title: Agrizy launches GenAI - powered formulation platform - The HinduBusinessLine
raw_text:
Agrizy, a tech-led contract research, development and manufacturing organisation (CRDMO) for global food and beverages and wellness brands, has introduced its proprietary GenAI-powered formulation platform that powers internal product development workflows.

A media statement said that the platform can turn product concepts into manufacturing-ready formulations in minutes, compressing typical new product development (NPD) cycles with respect to timelines and cost by up to 40 per cent.

Agrizy’s solution provides ranked formulation options along with ingredient quantities, costing insights, nutritional and allergen analysis, compliance validation, and export-ready lab documentation, enabling NPD teams to significantly accelerate product development workflows.

It said that the teams can define key product parameters such as category, packaging options, target cost, shelf life, formulation preferences, marketing claims, ingredient restrictions and sensory or performance profiles and receive actionable formulation outputs within minutes.

The platform also includes an integrated AI copilot that enables teams to formulate or re-formulate products using natural language instructions. This AI-assisted workflow allows continuous optimization across ingredients, claims, compliance requirements, nutrition profiles and end-use performance parameters, making the product development process faster, smarter, and significantly more iterative.

Every approved formulation feeds directly into Agrizy’s in-house labs, where real-world bench trial data, including yield, stability, sensory results and quality parameters continuously sharpen the AI’s recommendations. This ensures the system improves with every batch, not just every model update, the statement said.

The platform’s differentiation is built on three layers that are difficult to replicate: an India-specific ingredient ontology tagged with FSSAI, FDA and EFSA regulatory status; formulation memory that learns from failed combinations, not just successful ones; and constraint guardrails, it said.

Quoting Arun Markish, Co-Founder and CTO of Agrizy, the statement said the innovation in formulation science has traditionally depended on fragmented workflows, repeated manual experimentation and disconnected validation cycles.

“We engineered the system to solve core inefficiencies and unify ingredient ontology, formulation logic, regulatory constraints, and lab feedback into a single intelligence layer that continuously improves with every iteration. This allows research and development and product teams to simulate, refine and validate formulations with greater accuracy before moving into physical trials, significantly improving development efficiency, scalability and speed to market,” Markish said.

title: الصادرات السعودية غير النفطية ترتفع 19 % في 2025
raw_text:
الرياض – سجلت الصادرات السعودية غير النفطية، بما في ذلك إعادة التصدير، ارتفاعا بنسبة 18.9 في المائة في عام 2025 مقارنة بعام 2024، في حين انخفضت الصادرات الوطنية غير النفطية، باستثناء إعادة التصدير، بنسبة 0.1 في المائة.

وبحسب تقرير التجارة الدولية السلعية 2025، الذي نشرته الهيئة العامة للإحصاء، اليوم الأحد، ارتفعت الصادرات السلعية بنسبة 2.1 في المائة لتصل إلى 1170 مليار ريال، فيما انخفضت الصادرات النفطية بنسبة 4 في المائة.

وأظهر التقرير ارتفاع الواردات بنسبة 8.8 في المائة، لتصل إلى 949.8 مليار ريال، وانخفاض الفائض التجاري بنسبة 19.2 في المائة، ليتراجع إلى 220.2 مليار ريال مقارنة بعام 2024. وانخفضت حصة الصادرات النفطية من إجمالي الصادرات من 73.1 في المائة في عام 2024 إلى 68.7 في المائة في عام 2025.

وكشف التقرير عن زيادة بنسبة 64.4 بالمئة في قيمة السلع المعاد تصديرها العام الماضي. ويعزى ذلك إلى زيادة بنسبة 99.8 في المائة في الآلات والمعدات الكهربائية وأجزائها، والتي تمثل أكثر من 50 في المائة من إجمالي إعادة التصدير. وارتفعت نسبة الصادرات غير البترولية، بما في ذلك إعادة التصدير، إلى الواردات في عام 2025 لتصل إلى 38.5 في المائة مقارنة بـ 35.3 في المائة في عام 2024.

وشكلت المنتجات الكيماوية 22.5 في المائة من إجمالي الصادرات غير النفطية، مرتفعة بنسبة 4.7 في المائة العام الماضي مقارنة بعام 2024. تليها الآلات والمعدات الكهربائية وأجزائها، التي شكلت 22.4 في المائة من إجمالي الصادرات غير النفطية، مرتفعة بنسبة 91.8 في المائة العام الماضي.

وفي المقابل، أبرز السلع المستوردة الآلات والأجهزة الكهربائية والمعدات وأجزائها، والتي شكلت ما نسبته 29 في المائة من إجمالي الواردات بنسبة 24.6 في المائة، تليها معدات النقل وأجزائها التي شكلت 13.6 في المائة من إجمالي الواردات بنسبة 3.6 في المائة مقارنة بعام 2024.

وشكلت الصين الوجهة الأولى للصادرات السلعية للمملكة، حيث استحوذت على 14.6 في المائة من إجمالي الصادرات في عام 2025، تليها الإمارات بنسبة 10 في المائة، والهند بنسبة 9.4 في المائة. وجاءت كوريا الجنوبية واليابان والولايات المتحدة ومصر والبحرين وبولندا ومالطا ضمن أفضل 10 وجهات تصدير، حيث شكلت صادرات المملكة إلى هذه الدول العشر 66.8 في المائة من إجمالي صادراتها.

كما احتلت الصين المركز الأول بين الواردات السلعية للمملكة، حيث شكلت ما نسبته 27.5 في المائة من إجمالي الواردات في عام 2025. تليها الصين الولايات المتحدة بنسبة 8.2 في المائة، ثم الإمارات العربية المتحدة بنسبة 5.7 في المائة. وجاءت الهند، وألمانيا، واليابان، وإيطاليا، وفرنسا، وسويسرا، ومصر ضمن الدول العشر الأولى المصدرة، حيث يمثل إجمالي قيمة الواردات من هذه الدول العشر 65.9 بالمائة من إجمالي واردات المملكة.

وظل ميناء الملك عبد العزيز بالدمام البوابة الرئيسية للبضائع الداخلة إلى المملكة، حيث تعامل مع 26.6% من إجمالي الواردات العام الماضي. وجاء في المركز الثاني ميناء جدة الإسلامي بنسبة 22.1 في المائة، ثم مطار الملك خالد الدولي بالرياض بنسبة 13.8 في المائة، ومطار الملك عبد العزيز الدولي بجدة بنسبة 10.4 في المائة، ومطار الملك فهد الدولي بالدمام بنسبة 5.4 في المائة. وتشكل منافذ الدخول الخمسة هذه ما نسبته 78.2% من إجمالي الواردات السلعية للمملكة.

وبرز مطار الملك عبد العزيز الدولي بجدة كبوابة رئيسية لصادرات المملكة غير النفطية في عام 2025، حيث تعامل مع 14.2 في المائة من الإجمالي. يليه ميناء جدة الإسلامي بنسبة 11.7 في المائة، وميناء الملك فهد الصناعي بالجبيل بنسبة 11.1 في المائة، ومطار الملك خالد الدولي بالرياض بنسبة 10.6 في المائة، وميناء الجبيل بنسبة 7.9 في المائة. وشكلت هذه البوابات الخمس مجتمعة ما نسبته 55.4% من إجمالي الصادرات السلعية غير النفطية للمملكة.

صحفي محترف يتمتع بخبرة واسعة في مجال الإعلام، قاد العديد من المشاريع الإخبارية بنجاح. حاصل على تعليم جامعي عالٍ في تخصص الصحافة، ويتميز بالدقة والمصداقية في نقل الأخبار وتحرير المحتوى.

title: Apple Rolls Out Two Crucial Health Features For Apple Watch And AirPods In India
raw_text:
Apple has been on a spree of rolling out crucial health features to more people around the world. On May 12, it released the Hearing Aid features for AirPods Pro 2 and Pro 3 users in Italy, Romania, and Czechia. Now, it has announced the expansion of sleep apnoea notifications and the Hearing Test feature for the Apple Watch and AirPods Pro 2, respectively, in India.

Sleep apnoea is estimated to impact more than 1 billion people worldwide and, in most cases, goes undiagnosed. Detecting sleep disorders like sleep apnoea typically requires you to place sensors all over your body, but Apple managed to replicate this ability in a tiny wrist companion and get it cleared for use by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in 2024. It works by measuring movements in the wrist associated with breathing interruptions.

While the Apple Watch isn’t medical-grade equipment and can’t diagnose sleep disorders or replicate comprehensive sleep studies, it can help you figure out whether you should at least speak with a doctor about this condition. This is important because, if left untreated, it can increase the risk of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and cardiac issues.

Similarly, hearing loss often worsens gradually and can leave many people unaware that they may be living with the condition. Apple is rolling out the ability to get a clinical-grade Hearing Test, based on the standard clinical approach, for AirPods Pro 2 and Pro 3 users in India. While the Hearing Aid feature is yet to be released in the country, you can now take the Hearing Test in five minutes and get a summary of your results.

The sleep apnoea notifications feature is supported on Apple Watch Series 9 or later, Watch Ultra 2, or Watch SE 3 with the latest version of watchOS. Apple says the feature is intended for use by people 18 years or older who have not been diagnosed with sleep apnoea.

To enable sleep apnoea notifications on your Apple Watch, you need to:

Once set up, you’ll be able to view your sleep apnoea notifications or breathing disturbances in the Health app. If you receive a notification, you can also share a detailed report with your healthcare provider by scrolling down and tapping Export PDF.

Before you take the Hearing Test, you need to make sure your AirPods have a complete seal when placed in your ears. You can take the Ear Tip Fit Test to figure out the best silicone ear tip size. Once done, find a quiet place and follow these steps:

When done, you’ll see your hearing test results and any recommendations inside the Apple Health app. In the report, the higher the number, the louder the sounds need to be for you to hear them. For example, up to 25 dBHL indicates little to no hearing loss, whereas 26–40 dBHL indicates mild hearing loss. You can also see a detailed chart of your hearing level across the specific frequencies tested and export it as a PDF to share with your healthcare provider.

title: Lords Mark Industries Ltd . Introduces the First AI - powered integrated dialysis ecosystem in India .
raw_text:
All strata of renal care, smart technology to clinical processes to after discharge care, are now patient-centered. India's first indigenous smart hemodialysis ecosystem, live in Shakti Super Speciality Hospital, Ahmedabad

05 May, 2026, Mumbai: In a landmark move in renal care, Lord’s Mark Industries Ltd. has set up the, the first fully integrated AI-driven renal care ecosystem in Ahmedabad, India using the Lord’s Renal Renalyx Machine, the first smart hemodialysis system developed in India and the hardware base of an all-encompassing dialysis care ecosystem that combines AI clinical intelligence, operational management and remote patient monitoring.

The Renalex Machine is the physical platform of a larger unified ecosystem with AI-enhanced clinical intelligence on the RenalOS platform and end to end operational delivery on Aureoon, the Dialysis-as-a-Service model of Lord. The Renalyx Machine is designed and built in India with full certification of the CE, and this is a clear step towards no longer depending on imports but being able to build local machines on their own. A combination of these three layers enables Lords renal to establish, furnish, staff and run a fully controlled dialysis centre within a hospital with no capital input whatsoever on the part of the hospital partner, and make world-class renal care affordable and accessible at scale like never before.

The Lord Renal Renalyx is a machine whose design is based on a digital nephrology ecosystem which combines intelligent automation with clinical workflows. It allows to monitor treatment parameters in real-time, provide predictive alerts and data-driven decision support to minimize human error and enhance treatment consistency. Clinically, RenalOS provides the real time AI monitoring in all sessions, the ability to identify warning signs early, the ability to identify haemodynamic instability, and an increase in continuity of care beyond the centre by remote post-discharge monitoring. The outcome is the overhaul of episodic dialysis to a continuous, personalised, patient-centred renal care. Its cloud-based architecture enables distant monitoring, centralised data retrieval, and continuity of care throughout various sessions and areas. Lord’s is India first company to get Dilaysis machine Manufacturing licence in India

Manufacturing wise, the Lord Renal Renalyx Machine is the increased capacity of India to manufacture medical technologies that are relevant globally. It was developed in a Make in India framework and can be deployed faster, serviced easier and less dependent on operations, designed to fit Indian conditions and to scale the entire Lord Renal ecosystem model to the hospital networks in India and other developing markets. Lords Mark has set a bold plan of set up 50 Lords Renal managed dialysis centres within India by March 2027, domestic machine sales and an aggressive export programme.

The company is also trying to gain US FDA accreditation on the Lord’s Renal Renalyx Machine, which will further consolidate its global expansion strategy and its thrust to make India a destination of state-of-the-art dialysis.

Sachidanand Upadhyay, Managing Director, Lords Mark Industries Ltd., commented, this is one of the key AI-driven products in the larger technology portfolio of Lords, and we are determined to make India a worldwide leader in developing and manufacturing AI-based medical devices, our vision is to put India in the position of developing and producing a globally competitive dialysis technology platform.

As the need grows to provide long-term dialysis services in India and other developing economies, the centre of Shakti Super Speciality Hospital, Ahmedabad, illustrates how the completely integrated Lord Renal ecosystem can be used as the scalable solution to the next-generation dialysis delivery. Lord Renal has created a patient-first care delivery model to scale, one designed to serve both the population of emerging markets where reliable, quality renal care is of vital importance, and to establish India as a world leader in technology-driven, advanced kidney care by incorporating clinical intelligence via RenalOS, operational delivery via Aureoon, and native hardware via the Renalyx Machine.

Lord Marks Industries Ltd. is a manufacturer of products that are distributed in the marketplace.

Lords Mark Industries Ltd. is an Indian diversified conglomerate, which was established in 1998 with its headquarters in Mumbai and it deals with healthcare, diagnostics, renewable energy and printing and packaging. The company listed on BSE has developed a list of businesses that are in line with national priorities such as Make in India, Smart Cities, and accessible healthcare with partners such as Cipla, Philips and Hindustan Antibiotics.

The healthcare portfolio of the Lords Mark includes diagnostics and medical technology with LordsMed, its GMP-WHO compliant IVD manufacturing facility, surgical products with Lords Surgical, and AI-based renal care with Lords Renal, its patient-centered integrated dialysis ecosystem with indigenous hardware, clinical intelligence and managed operations, to make the world-leading dialysis accessible and affordable at scale.

With a desire to have a world renowned brand in varying industries, Lords mark has increased its presence in the international arena with Lords Global in USA and is also seeking strategic alliances in Asia and Africa. Dr. Sachidanand Upadhyay, the Managing Director and the CEO, heads the company.

To find out more visit http://www.lordsmark.com/.

title: Indian pharma sites see fewer USFDA official actions in FY26 even as surprise inspections expand
raw_text:
Indian pharmaceutical manufacturing sites saw fewer US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) enforcement actions in fiscal 2026, with Official Action Indicated (OAI) findings more than halving year‑on‑year.  The USFDA conducted 212 drug facility inspections in 2025, down from 284 in 2024 in India, reflecting a decline in inspection volume, For India, Official Action Indicated (OAI) outcomes fell to three in FY26 from seven in FY25, USFDA classifies a facility for Official Action Indicated (OAI) if it finds serious violations. OAI blocks new approvals in the US and sometimes disrupts production.

The US remains the most critical overseas market for Indian drugmakers, accounting for around one‑third to 40 percent of their revenues, driven largely by generic medicines and complex formulations.

The decline has unfolded alongside the agency’s move to expand unannounced foreign inspections, a policy intended to tighten oversight and eliminate inspection‑day compliance fixes. Unannounced inspections, introduced more broadly for foreign drugmakers from May 2025, have altered how facilities are assessed rather than what is assessed.

Unlike pre‑announced audits, surprise visits capture routine manufacturing behaviour—batch handling, deviation responses, data controls and investigation practices as they operate day‑to‑day. Facilities that rely on short‑term corrective actions are more likely to face enforcement, while those with embedded quality systems tend to perform consistently regardless of inspection notice.

In India, a widening group of large export‑oriented manufacturers appears to fall into the latter category. After a decade marked by warning letters and import alerts, many companies have strengthened quality governance, hired experts into compliance leadership, and standardised systems across global operations.

These changes reduce the probability that inspectors will find systemic, enforcement‑level failures that trigger OAIs, even when inspections are unannounced.

The outcome reflects structural changes inside Indian drug plants rather than a softer regulatory approach, said Joseph Ryan Lambert, Vice President of Global Corporate Quality Assurance at Biocon and a former USFDA field inspector.

“Unannounced inspections don’t change the standards—they change what inspectors actually see,” Lambert said. “If quality systems are working every day, not just on inspection days, facilities tend to hold up even when there’s no advance notice.”

Lambert, who spent nearly two decades with the USFDA inspecting drug facilities globally before joining Biocon, said enforcement outcomes increasingly hinge on whether companies maintain consistent investigation discipline.

“The most common and serious issue I saw—worldwide, not just in India—was failing to extend investigations,” he said.

“When something goes wrong, the expectation is that firms assess whether batches already on the market could be affected. That’s a key FDA focus area, and where inspections often escalate.”

According to Lambert, Indian manufacturers that have adopted a single, global quality framework are better positioned under surprise inspections. “We don’t operate different quality systems for different geographies,” he said. “There’s one quality standard, one oversight model, regardless of whether a product is shipped to the US or anywhere else. That consistency reduces regulatory risk.”

At the same time, the USFDA’s enforcement mix has evolved. While OAIs have declined, Voluntary Action Indicated (VAI) outcomes have risen, suggesting inspectors are still identifying deficiencies but judging them to be correctable without formal enforcement. This reflects a regulatory preference to reserve OAIs for cases involving data integrity breakdowns, unresolved investigation failures or risks to marketed product—rather than procedural gaps that firms can plausibly remediate.

Capacity constraints at the USFDA may also be a contributing factor. Workforce reductions and internal restructuring in early 2025 strained inspection resources, particularly for foreign sites. While the agency has reaffirmed its commitment to surprise inspections, fewer inspectors mean greater reliance on risk‑based prioritisation. In such a framework, facilities with stable compliance histories are less likely to face repeat or escalation‑level scrutiny, limiting the pool of sites that could generate OAIs.

Crucially, the drop in OAIs does not signal reduced regulatory pressure. Unannounced inspections raise the baseline expectation for continuous compliance and narrow the margin for error.

title: Informa Markets Puts Bangkok at the Center of Southeast Asia Pharma Industry , Uniting 400 Exhibitors , Experts from 70 Countries at CPHI South East Asia
raw_text:
The Region's Premier Pharma Exhibition Returns to Bangkok, Elevating Thailand's Role in the ASEAN Pharmaceutical Supply Chain

BANGKOK, May 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Informa Markets sets to organise CPHI South East Asia from 8-10 July 2026 at Queen Sirikit National Convention Center under the theme "The Gateway to the ASEAN Pharma Industry." The event is a comprehensive pharmaceutical manufacturing exhibition, technology showcase, and conference for Southeast Asia, featuring innovations from more than 400 companies worldwide.

Highlights include international pavilion zones from eight markets, showcasing innovation trends from Mainland China, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, Vietnam, and Egypt. The event will also provide business matching opportunities and over 60 academic conference sessions. Organisers expect more than 10,000 visitors from over 70 countries during the three-day event, creating new business opportunities throughout the exhibition.

CPHI South East Asia 2026 hosts an official press conference in Bangkok, announcing the return of Southeast Asia's premier pharmaceutical exhibition to Queen Sirikit National Convention Center, 8-10 July 2026. The event will bring together over 400 exhibitors and 10,000 visitors from 70+ countries under the theme "The Gateway to the ASEAN Pharma Industry."

In 2024, Thailand's pharmaceutical industry was valued at approximately THB 240 billion (around 6.9 billion dollars), and is projected to grow by 6-7% due to these supporting factors. Market research agencies also forecast that by 2030, the industry could reach a value of 480 billion baht or 13.9 billion dollars.

Industry and government leaders take part in a panel discussion at the CPHI South East Asia 2026 press conference, highlighting Thailand's role as the region's pharmaceutical manufacturing hub.

Pharmaceutical and healthcare security has therefore become a national policy priority aimed at raising public healthcare standards and strengthening the country's economy as Thailand seeks to join the OECD within five years. Policies also focus on reducing reliance on imported medicines, supporting domestic active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) production, and increasing manufacturing capacity for essential medicines in line with actual production costs.

This is the driving force behind the organization of CPHI South East Asia, a technology and innovation exhibition with the important goal of contributing to Thailand's pharmaceutical security. The event aims to help drive both healthcare and the economy forward, positioning Thailand as a Medical Hub for Southeast Asia through internationally standardized pharmaceutical manufacturing and enhanced competitiveness in global export markets.

Food and Drug Administration Office (Thai FDA), Thai Pharmaceutical Manufacturers Association (TPMA), Government Pharmaceutical Organization (GPO),industry leaders gather at the CPHI South East Asia 2026 press conference in Bangkok, united in advancing Thailand's position as Southeast Asia's leading Medical Hub.

"CPHI South East Asia is part of International Healthcare Week and will be held at Queen Sirikit National Convention Center from 8-10 July 2026 under the theme "The Gateway to the ASEAN Pharma Industry." The event will contribute to advancing Thailand's pharmaceutical industry in line with the country's strategic development goals."

Ms. Supatra Boonserm, Secretary-General of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), under the Food and Drug Administration Office (Thai FDA), Ministry of Public Health, stated that in a world where medical technology continues to advance rapidly, we are now entering the era of Advanced Therapy Medicinal Products (ATMPs). These are no longer just "medicines" in the traditional sense, but represent "new hope" for treating diseases once considered incurable - whether through cell therapy, gene therapy, or tissue engineering.

Today, the role of the Thai FDA is no longer limited to being merely a "regulator" responsible for screening product safety. It has evolved into an "Innovation Facilitator," aiming to position Thailand as a true regional healthcare hub. The FDA's key mission in supporting ATMPs is built upon three major pillars:

1.Creating a Regulatory "Fast Track" (Regulatory Excellence)

Complex innovations require regulations that are both flexible and rigorous. The FDA has therefore developed legal frameworks aligned with international standards, covering product classification and dedicated GMP standards specifically for ATMPs. This ensures that products developed by Thai innovators meet global standards and can confidently compete in international markets.

2. Serving as a Strategic Partner for Researchers and Entrepreneurs (Proactive Partnership)

The FDA has implemented a Pre-submission Consultation mechanism to provide technical guidance before formal approval applications are submitted. It has also introduced Fast Track pathways for products addressing urgent medical needs, helping reduce unnecessary delays and barriers while maintaining patient safety as the highest priority.

3. Building an "Ecosystem of Trust" (Ecosystem of Trust)

The FDA oversees clinical trials to ensure ethical compliance and maintains long-term post-market safety monitoring systems. This is intended to build confidence among both patients and healthcare professionals that these innovations will remain effective and safe in a sustainable manner.

Mr. Surachai Ruengsuksilp, Honorary Chairman of the Pharmaceutical Industry Group under the Federation of Thai Industries and Vice President of the Thai Pharmaceutical Manufacturers Association (TPMA), stated that the pharmaceutical industry is not merely an economic driver, but also a "critical infrastructure for national security."

Currently, Thailand's pharmaceutical market is valued at more than THB 240 billion. Amid these opportunities, the Federation of Thai Industries has established a strategic direction to position Thailand as a full-fledged Regional Pharma Hub through three key strategies:

1.Transforming from an "Importer" to a "Producer for Security"

Reducing dependence on imported medicines by promoting domestic production of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs), thereby reducing vulnerability to global crises.

2. Upgrading from "Basic Medicines" to "Advanced Innovation"

Supporting Thai pharmaceutical manufacturers in upgrading to internationally recognized PIC/S GMP standards, enabling Thai medicines not only to serve the CLMV market but also to expand exports globally.

3. Building a Strong Pharmaceutical Ecosystem

Driving collaboration with the government and the Board of Investment (BOI) to create an investment environment conducive to research and development, while also reforming procurement regulations to better reflect actual quality-based costs. This is intended to help Thai pharmaceutical companies remain competitive and achieve sustainable growth.

The Federation of Thai Industries aims to make Thailand "a regional production base for high-quality and affordable medicines," focusing not only on economic growth figures, but also on ensuring that Thai people have sufficient access to safe medicines under all circumstances.

Dr.Ponthip Wirachwong Ph.D. Deputy Managing Director, Government Pharmaceutical Organization (GPO), stated that beyond its primary role in pharmaceutical manufacturing, the organization's core mission is to ensure confidence in Thailand's healthcare system by guaranteeing that Thai people will never face medicine shortages during crises or at any time.

In the past, Thailand has experienced epidemics and natural disasters, and the GPO has maintained reserve systems for essential medicines and medical supplies to ensure that hospital operations can continue without disruption caused by delays.

"Even the most advanced medicine fails if it remains out of reach. GPO's mission is simple: ensure every Thai patient has access to safe, quality medicines - at a price that doesn't force them to choose between health and survival," she said.

Pre-registration is now open for visitors and exhibitors. Be part of the future of ASEAN's pharma industry at www.cphi.com/sea

title: We can see Pharmaceutical Industry doubling in next five years : Piyush Goyal
raw_text:
ANI
                09 Jun 2026, 00:04 GMT+10

New Delhi [India], June 8 (ANI): Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Monday expressed strong confidence in India's pharmaceutical sector, saying the country's USD 60 billion pharmaceutical Industry is poised to double in next five years as he addressed the Pharmaceutical Export Promotion Council's Global Ambassadors Meet on the sidelines of IPHEX 2025, the 12th edition of India's premier pharma and healthcare exhibition.

Goyal outlined three pillars defining India's pharmaceutical strength.

First, trust. India has aligned its Good Manufacturing Practices framework with global benchmarks, produces 65-70% of the World Health Organisation's vaccine requirements, and hosts the largest number of US FDA-approved plants of any country in the world. Ten out of 25 global generic companies operate out of India.

Second, innovation. Patent filings have nearly doubled in recent years. The government has launched Biopharma Shakti to encourage domestic pharmaceutical innovation and has committed a USD 10 billion fund to support innovation accross sector, including pharma. Goyal noted that due to India's significantly lower cost of operations, this investment carries the effective weight of roughly $100 billion in a country like Switzerland.

'You can probably get the same talent at one-tenth the price in India, and serve global innovation needs from here,' he said.

Third, partnership. Goyal invited global pharma companies to set up operations in India, citing the pull of 1.4 billion consumers, a rising middle class, and the world's fastest-growing large economy. He pointed out that India recorded GDP growth of 7.7% at constant prices for the year ended March 2026, even amid 50% US tariffs and two ongoing global conflicts.

Goyal underscored the irreplaceable role of Indian generics in global healthcare, noting that 80-90% of medicines sold in the US by volume are generics, many sourced from India.

'If generics were not available at the price points that India offers, millions of patients around the world would have had to suffer lack of access to medicine,' he said, adding that India intends to move further into innovative and high-value pharmaceutical segments without compromising its generic strength.

Reflecting on the pandemic years, Goyal praised the Indian pharma industry's resilience and described how India ensured equitable global access to medicines and vaccines during COVID-19.

Over 100 countries received medicines from India free of charge, and paying nations were supplied at pre-COVID prices, with deliberate measures taken to prevent traders from cornering supplies and profiteering.

'That was the sensitivity with which we managed the COVID period,' he said.

New Delhi [India], June 8 (ANI): Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Monday expressed strong confidence in India's pharmaceutical sector, saying the country's USD 60 billion pharmaceutical Industry is poised to double in next five years as he addressed the Pharmaceutical Export Promotion Council's Global Ambassadors Meet on the sidelines of IPHEX 2025, the 12th edition of India's premier pharma and healthcare exhibition.

Goyal outlined three pillars defining India's pharmaceutical strength.

First, trust. India has aligned its Good Manufacturing Practices framework with global benchmarks, produces 65-70% of the World Health Organisation's vaccine requirements, and hosts the largest number of US FDA-approved plants of any country in the world. Ten out of 25 global generic companies operate out of India.

Second, innovation. Patent filings have nearly doubled in recent years. The government has launched Biopharma Shakti to encourage domestic pharmaceutical innovation and has committed a USD 10 billion fund to support innovation accross sector, including pharma. Goyal noted that due to India's significantly lower cost of operations, this investment carries the effective weight of roughly $100 billion in a country like Switzerland.

'You can probably get the same talent at one-tenth the price in India, and serve global innovation needs from here,' he said.

Third, partnership. Goyal invited global pharma companies to set up operations in India, citing the pull of 1.4 billion consumers, a rising middle class, and the world's fastest-growing large economy. He pointed out that India recorded GDP growth of 7.7% at constant prices for the year ended March 2026, even amid 50% US tariffs and two ongoing global conflicts.

Goyal underscored the irreplaceable role of Indian generics in global healthcare, noting that 80-90% of medicines sold in the US by volume are generics, many sourced from India.

'If generics were not available at the price points that India offers, millions of patients around the world would have had to suffer lack of access to medicine,' he said, adding that India intends to move further into innovative and high-value pharmaceutical segments without compromising its generic strength.

Reflecting on the pandemic years, Goyal praised the Indian pharma industry's resilience and described how India ensured equitable global access to medicines and vaccines during COVID-19.

title: From apples to apparels : Who gains what in the India – New Zealand FTA
raw_text:
The India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement, signed on April 27, secures 100 percent duty-free access for Indian exports to New Zealand while carefully calibrating New Delhi's own tariff concessions to protect sensitive sectors.

Negotiated in a record nine months after being announced in March 2025, the FTA is expected to boost trade in goods and services between India and New Zealand, which reached $2.4 billion in 2024, with merchandise trade in FY2024–25 at $1.3 billion, marking a 49 percent increase over the previous year.

New Zealand’s across-the-board elimination of tariffs, covering more than 8,000 tariff lines, will immediately benefit a wide range of Indian sectors, particularly labour-intensive industries.

The government said the move will “enhance competitiveness in labour-intensive sectors such as textiles, apparel, leather, footwear, gems and jewellery,” placing MSMEs and job creation at the centre of the agreement’s gains.

Agricultural products including honey, spices, cereals, fruits, coffee and cocoa are also expected to gain from improved market access, widening the export base beyond traditional sectors.

Textiles and apparel are expected to be among the biggest beneficiaries, spanning garments, home textiles and handloom products, while leather and footwear exporters, previously facing tariffs of up to 10 percent, will enter the New Zealand market duty-free once the agreement is implemented.

Gems and jewellery exporters also stand to gain a pricing advantage in a high-income market, alongside engineering goods, plastics and other manufactured products that will benefit from tariff elimination.

In agriculture and food products, several Indian exports will now enjoy improved access, including honey, spices, cereals, fruits, coffee and cocoa—segments where tariff removal is expected to boost competitiveness and open up new opportunities for farmers and food processors.

The inclusion of honey is particularly significant, as it signals market access for niche agri-exports and value-added products beyond traditional bulk commodities.

While India has secured comprehensive access abroad, its own tariff commitments remain measured.

India has offered tariff liberalisation on 70.03 percent of tariff lines covering 95 percent of bilateral trade value, while keeping 29.97 percent of tariff lines in exclusion to protect India's sensitive sectors.

The country will eliminate duties on around 30 percent of tariff lines immediately, with phased reductions on another 35.6 percent, largely in areas that support domestic industry. These include inputs such as wool, forestry products, sheep meat and coal.

Market access for select New Zealand agricultural products such as apples, kiwifruit, Mānuka honey and albumins, including milk albumin, will be governed through tariff rate quotas (TRQs) combined with minimum import prices and safeguard measures.

Overall, just 0.06 percent of tariff lines fall under these TRQs.

For Mānuka honey, which currently attracts a 66 percent duty, imports from New Zealand stand at 14.2 MT (valued at $0.3 million) compared to 356.8 MT globally. The agreement allows an in-quota TRQ of 200 MT per year with a minimum import price of $20/kg and a 75 percent tariff reduction over five years, while out-of-quota imports will be subject to a higher minimum import price of $30/kg with similar phased tariff cuts. Duties will decline progressively from 56.1 percent in the first year to 16.5 percent from the fifth year onwards.

In the case of apples, which currently face a 50 percent duty, imports from New Zealand stand at 31,392.6 MT ($32.4 million) out of total imports of over 519,000 MT. The agreement provides an in-quota TRQ starting at 32,500 MT in year one and rising to 45,000 MT by year six, with a reduced duty of 25 percent and a minimum import price of $1.25/kg during a defined seasonal window.

For kiwifruit, currently taxed at 33 percent, imports from New Zealand stand at 5,840 MT ($16.9 million). The TRQ begins at 6,250 MT in year one and expands to 15,000 MT by year six, with zero duty within quota and a minimum import price of $1.80/kg, while out-of-quota imports remain subject to higher duties and pricing safeguards.

Similarly, albumins, including milk albumin, currently taxed at 22 percent, will see an in-quota TRQ of 1,000 MT in year one rising to 3,000 MT by year five at a concessional duty of 11 percent, with out-of-quota imports continuing at prevailing rates.

These TRQs are paired with Agriculture Productivity Action Plans and will be monitored by a Joint Agriculture Productivity Council, ensuring that increased market access is balanced with domestic sector protection and productivity improvements.

New Zealand wine gets price-based tariff cuts, not a TRQ.

Wine priced below $5 per 750 ml bottle gets no concession and stays at 150 percent duty.

Those priced between US$5 and $15 gets duty reduced to 100 percent at entry into force, and then gradually to 50 percent by Year 10.

Wine priced at $15 or more gets a sharper cut, from 150 percent to 75 percent at entry into force, and then to 25 percent by Year 10.

At the same time, India has drawn firm red lines around its most sensitive sectors. Dairy, edible oils, sugar and key agricultural commodities are excluded from tariff concessions, ensuring protection for farmers and rural livelihoods.

Beyond goods, the agreement makes significant advances in services and mobility. For the first time in any bilateral agreement, New Zealand has created a dedicated pathway on student mobility and post-study work visas for India.

The deal removes numerical caps on Indian students, guarantees a minimum of 20 hours of work per week during study, and provides extended post-study work opportunities of up to three years for STEM bachelor’s and master’s graduates and up to four years for doctoral graduates.

Youth mobility is also enhanced through multiple-entry working holiday visas for 1,000 young Indians annually, valid for 12 months, aimed at promoting skills development and people-to-people linkages.

In pharmaceuticals and medical devices, the agreement streamlines regulatory access by enabling acceptance of GMP and GCP inspection reports from trusted global regulators such as the US FDA, EMA, UK MHRA and Health Canada. This is expected to reduce duplicative inspections, lower compliance costs and accelerate product approvals, facilitating smoother market access for Indian exporters.

On intellectual property, New Zealand has committed to amending its geographical indications (GI) law within 18 months of the agreement’s entry into force. Currently limited to wines and spirits, the revised framework will allow registration of Indian GIs across a wider range of products, extending treatment similar to that accorded to the European Union and opening the door for protection of iconic Indian goods in the New Zealand market.

The agreement also carries a proposed $20 billion investment commitment from New Zealand over 15 years, along with cooperation in areas such as agriculture, skills and services, which is expected to deepen bilateral ties beyond trade. This commitment comes with a Rebalancing Clause to address any shortfall in investment delivery.

Both countries have also agreed to work towards linking fast payment systems, aimed at enabling quicker, low-cost cross-border transactions and facilitating trade and remittances.

title: « معلومات الوزراء »: 12 مليار دولار قيمة الصادرات غير البترولية بزيادة 7 . 1 %
raw_text:
أصدر مركز المعلومات ودعم اتخاذ القرار بمجلس الوزراء، العدد 20 من تقرير "الصادرات السلعية غير البترولية"، وهي إصدارة ربع سنوية تتناول نظرة عامة على هيكل الميزان التجار غير البترولي المصري خلال الفترة (الربع الرابع 2024 - الربع الرابع 2025)، بالإضافة إلى تطور الصادرات السلعية غير البترولية عن الفترة المذكورة، كما تتناول عرضًا للعلاقات التجارية بين مصر وأهم الشركاء التجاريين خلال الفترة (الربع الرابع 2024 - الربع الرابع 2025).

وبلغت قيمة صادرات مصر من السلع غير البترولية 12 مليار دولار خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025 مقابل نحو 11.2 مليار دولار خلال الربع نفسه من عام 2024، بنسبة ارتفاع بلغت نحو 7.1%.

فيما بلغت قيمة الواردات المصرية من السلع غير البترولية 23.3 مليار دولار خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025، مقابل نحو 21.2 مليار دولار خلال الربع نفسه من عام 2024، بنسبة ارتفاع بلغت نحو 9.9%، وفقاً لبيانات الهيئة العامة للرقابة على الصادرات والواردات.

واستعرض التقرير تطور قيمة الصادرات المصرية من السلع غير البترولية وفقًا لأعلى مجموعات السلع تصديرًا خلال الربع الرابع 2025، حيث جاءت مجموعة اللؤلؤ الطبيعي أو المستنبت والأحجار الكريمة في مقدمة الصادرات المصرية من السلع غير البترولية من حيث القيمة خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025، وذلك بنحو 1.3 مليار دولار مقابل نحو 1.1 مليار دولار خلال الربع نفسه من عام 2024، تلتها صادرات مجموعة الآلات والأجهزة والمعدات الكهربائية وأجزاؤها بقيمة 891.1 مليون دولار خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025، مقابل نحو 764.3 مليون دولار خلال الربع نفسه من عام 2024.

ولفت تقرير مركز المعلومات إلى أنه من بين أعلى 10 مجموعات سلعية تصديرًا خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025 ارتفع الوزن النسبي لبعض المجموعات السلعية غير البترولية مقارنًة بالربع نفسه من عام 2024، وهم: مجموعة اللؤلؤ الطبيعي أو المستنبت والأحجار الكريمة (من 9.6% إلى 11%)، ومجموعة الآلات والأجهزة والمعدات الكهربائية وأجزاؤها (من 6.9% إلى 7.5%)، ومجموعة الفواكه والثمار القشرية الصالحة للأكل وقشور الحمضيات (من 5.4% إلى 6%)، ومجموعة الملح والكبريت والمواد الجبسية (من 3.5% إلى 3.6%).

مقابل انخفاض الوزن النسبي لبعض المجموعات من السلع غير البترولية خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025، مقارنًة بالربع نفسه من عام 2024، وهم: مجموعة الأسمدة (من 6.3% إلى 5.9%)، ومجموعة اللدائن ومصنوعاتها (من 6% إلى 5.4%)، ومجموعة الوقود المعدني والزيوت المعدنية ومنتجات تقطيرها (من 5.5% إلى 4.1%)، ومجموعة الخضر والنباتات والجذور والدرنات الصالحة للأكل (من 3.9% إلى 3.4%)، ومجموعة الحديد الصب (الظهر) والحديد والصلب (الفولاذ) (من 6.2% إلى 3.4%).

وفيما يتعلق بأكثر المجموعات السلعية التي ارتفعت صادراتها، جاءت مجموعة اللؤلؤ الطبيعي أو المستنبت والأحجار الكريمة في مقدمة المجموعات السلعية التي ارتفعت صادرات مصر منها حيث سجلت قيمتها نحو 1318.5 مليون دولار خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025، مقابل نحو 1073.7 مليون دولار خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2024، بزيادة قدرها 244.8 مليون دولار، وجاءت مجموعة الآلات والأجهزة والمعدات الكهربائية وأجزاؤها في المرتبة الثانية، حيث سجلت قيمة صادرات مصر منها نحو 891.1 مليون دولار خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025، مقارنًة بنحو 764.3 مليون دولار خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2024، بزيادة قدرها 126.8 مليون دولار، وجاءت مجموعة الفواكه والثمار القشرية الصالحة للأكل في المرتبة الثالثة، حيث سجلت قيمة صادرات مصر منها 714.4 مليون دولار خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025، مقابل 596.9 مليون دولار خلال الربع الرابع 2024، بزيادة قدرها 117.5 مليون دولار.

من بين المجموعات السلعية التي ارتفعت صادرات مصر منها -على أساس سنوي- خلال الربع الرابع 2025 تستحوذ مجموعة اللؤلؤ الطبيعي أو المستنبت والأحجار الكريمة على النصيب الأكبر من إجمالي قيمة صادرات المجموعات السلعية، وذلك بنسبة 11%، تليها مجموعة الآلات والأجهزة والمعدات الكهربائية وأجزاؤها بنسبة 7.5%.

أما فيما يتعلق بالمجموعات السلعية التي انخفضت صادراتها، فقد جاءت مجموعة الحديد الصب (الظهر) والحديد والصلب (الفولاذ) على رأس قائمة المجموعات السلعية التي انخفضت صادرات مصر منها لتسجل نحو 408.3 ملايين دولار خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025، مقابل نحو 692 مليون دولار خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2024، بانخفاض قدره 283.7 مليون دولار، وجاءت مجموعة الوقود المعدني والزيوت المعدنية ومنتجات تقطيرها في المرتبة الثانية، حيث سجلت قيمة الصادرات منها نحو 494.1 مليون دولار خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025 مقابل نحو 610.1 ملايين دولار خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2024، بانخفاض قدره 116 مليون دولار، وجاءت مجموعة النحاس ومصنوعاته في المرتبة الثالثة، حيث سجلت قيمة الصادرات منها نحو 240.8 مليون دولار خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025، مقابل نحو 296.5 مليون دولار خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2024، بانخفاض قدره 55.7 مليون دولار.

من بين المجموعات السلعية التي انخفضت صادرات مصر منها -على أساس سنوي- خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025، تستحوذ مجموعة اللدائن ومصنوعاتها على النصيب الأكبر من إجمالي قيمة صادرات المجموعات السلعية بنسبة 5.4%، تليها مجموعة الوقود المعدني والزيوت المعدنية ومنتجات تقطيرها بنسبة 4.1%.

وأشار تقرير مركز المعلومات ودعم اتخاذ القرار إلى أبرز الدول المستوردة للسلع المصرية غير البترولية خلال الربع الرابع 2025، حيث جاءت الإمارات العربية المتحدة كأكبر مستورد للسلع المصرية غير البترولية خلال الفترة المذكورة بقيمة 1.1 مليار دولار وهو ما يمثل 9.4% من إجمالي الصادرات المصرية من السلع غير البترولية، تلتها تركيا بقيمة 820.6 مليون دولار وبنسبة 6.9% من إجمالي الصادرات المصرية من السلع غير البترولية، ثم المملكة العربية السعودية في المرتبة الثالثة بقيمة 783.3 مليون دولار وبنسبة 6.6% من إجمالي الصادرات المصرية من السلع غير البترولية.

وأوضح المركز أبرز الفرص التصديرية غير المستغلة للصادرات المصرية من السلع غير البترولية، فوفقًا لتقديرات مركز التجارة العالمي لعام 2030، تمتلك مصر قدرات تصديرية في بعض السلع تبلغ نحو 32 مليار دولار إلا أنها غير مستغلة، ويتمثل أبرز تلك السلع في الذهب الخام غير المشغول لأغراض غير نقدية واليوريا والبرتقال، وتظهر سلعة الذهب الخام غير المشغول لأغراض غير نقدية أكبر فرق مطلق بين الصادرات المحتملة والصادرات الفعلية من حيث القيمة، مما يترك مجالًا لتعزيز قيمة الصادرات منه بنحو 2.2 مليار دولار وهو ما يمثل 6.8% من إمكانات التصدير غير المستغلة خاصًة وأن الذهب الخام غير المشغول لأغراض غير نقدية يُعد المنتج الذي يواجه أقوى طلب محتمل على مستوى العالم.

وبخصوص الفرص التصديرية غير المستغلة للصادرات المصرية في كبرى الأسواق، أوضح التقرير أن الولايات المتحدة الأمريكية تعد أكبر سوق لمصر من حيث فرص التصدير غير المستغلة بقيمة 2.8 مليار دولار وبما يمثل نحو 8.8% من إمكانات مصر التصديرية غير المستغلة والمقدرة بنحو 32 مليار دولار، تليها تركيا بنحو 1.9 مليار دولار.

تناول التقرير أهم الشركاء التجاريين لمصر خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025، حيث جاءت الصين الشعبية كأهم الشركاء بقيمة تبادل تجاري بلغت 5.7 مليارات دولار خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025، تلتها الولايات المتحدة الأمريكية، والإمارات العربية المتحدة بقيمة تبادل تجاري بلغت 2.2 مليار دولار لكل منهما، ثم البرازيل بقيمة 1.8 مليار دولار، وتركيا وألمانيا الاتحادية بقيمة تبادل تجاري بلغت 1.6 مليار دولار لكل منهما، وإيطاليا 1.5 مليار دولار، والمملكة العربية السعودية بقيمة بلغت 1.4 مليار دولار، والهند بقيمة 1.1 مليار دولار.

كما تناول تقرير مركز المعلومات الميزان التجاري غير البترولي بين مصر وأهم الشركاء التجاريين خلال الربع الرابع من 2025 عام، حيث جاءت الصين في مقدمة الدول التي حققت مصر معها عجزًا تجاريًا خلال الفترة المشار إليها بقيمة عجز تجاري بلغ 5.43 مليارات دولار، تلتها البرازيل بقيمة 1.32 مليار دولار، ثم روسيا الاتحادية بقيمة 1.30 مليار دولار، وارتفع العجز التجاري لمصر مع الصين بمقدار 1.2 مليار دولار خلال الربع الرابع 2025 مقارنًة بالربع نفسه من عام 2024، في حين تراجع قيمة العجز التجاري لمصر مع السويد، وكوريا الجنوبية بنحو 47.8 مليون دولار و 21.6 مليون دولار على التوالي خلال الربع الرابع 2025، مقارنًة بالربع نفسه من عام 2024.

واتصالًا، جاءت ليبيا في مقدمة الدول التي حققت مصر معها فائضًا في الميزان التجاري غير البترولي خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025 بقيمة بلغت نحو 422.7 مليون دولار، مقارنًة بفائض قدره 504 ملايين دولار خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2024، وتجدر الإشارة إلى أن تسع دول من أكبر عشر دول حققت مصر معها فائض في الميزان التجاري غير البترولي خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025 هي دول عربية، كما ارتفعت قيمة الفائض في الميزان التجاري غير البترولي لمصر مع سويسرا بنحو 196.7 مليون دولار خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025، لتسجل نحو 334.5 مليون دولار، مقارنًة بنحو 137.8 مليون دولار خلال الربع نفسه من عام 2024.

title: India Manufacturing Boom Fuels Surge in Demand for Foreign Language Interpreters & Localisation Services
raw_text:
ANI |
 Updated: May 29, 2026 13:35  IST

VMPLNew Delhi [India], May 29: As India established itself as the new manufacturing capital of the world, a fledgling parallel industry was emerging. National companies were setting up manufacturing bases, R&D centers, and full supply chains; however, the people within did not speak the same language.Technical is the very foundation of the manufacturing industry. One wrongly translated word in the equipment guide, safety rule, or spec of the machine could be a risk for any mass production system or even everyone working in the factory. This situation generates a huge progress in technical translation services. Then, the needs of the know-how translators to do technical reports translation, business negotiations, accommodation, or proper official documents authentication are expanding.What Is the Role of Market Research Translation in Understanding Global Buyers?Language-related problems faced by companies at the first step of internationalization. Prior to exporting a product to a non-English-speaking country, companies must undertake extensive consumer and competitor analyses, thus emphasizing the importance of market research translation. Indian manufacturers are consequently translating consumer surveys, focus group dialogue, and competitive intelligence reports from languages such as Japanese, Spanish, German, and French through the work of language experts. When expressed into English or Indian tongues through Indian translators, the sales decisions, pricing trends, and statute-compliance can be correctly understood by companies that can then ensure that their home concept exports successfully.How Does Precision in Technical Translation Services Protect Heavy Industries?The translator is as accurate as the equipment. While translating an equipment manual, safety procedure, or even a machinery specification, one mistaken word can spell doom. It can bring down entire production lines or cause safety concerns. Hence, the skies are haunted by inflated demands for translator services. Japanese, Korean, and German engineers often work with the Indian engineers in the factory premises. User guides, maintenance guides, and software interfaces need to be translated to be the same; they are constantly opting for language providers. Translation agencies say there is a huge rise in demands from Chinese, Italian, and Russian technical, industrial, and heavy-duty machinery translations.What Role Do Business and Legal Translation Services Play in Navigating Cross-Border Agreements?

As transnational cooperation and cross-border transactions become the new way of life, countries need more than simple caution. India is witnessing increased distribution, technology transfer, and non-disclosure agreements with foreign companies. To minimise any possible litigation costs, the provision of a full range of business and legal translation services is becoming an essential part of doing business. The professional in this field of legal translation services provides critical support for supply chain transactions, articles of agreement, terms of business, employee policies, arbitration documents, etc. Available in English and in languages like Arabic, Portuguese, Thai, etc.When Are Certified Translation Services Required to Meet Compliance Standards?Official, professionally certified translations are often demanded by government tenders, import-export paperwork, and other official submissions. This is where certified translation services come in. A dot on the signature line from a certified translator, attesting to the veracity of the translation, can prove crucial when the Indian auto parts manufacturer - having secured a contract with a European manufacturer - puts the requisite multitude of documentation, from factory quality assurance to pollution checks, before the authorities in the EU; or when the pharmaceutical company seeking US FDA approval needs not just sterilization logs, but also certified translations. As Indian manufacturing enterprises face increased scrutiny from foreign auditors and a greater need for Dutch, Swedish, or Polish interpreter and translator skills, the demand for certified translators continues to grow noticeably.Why Are On-Site Interpreters Becoming Essential in Smart Factories?In addition to written translations, the market for spoken language assistance is also flourishing. Around Indian factory floors now are crews from a range of different countries. A Korean assembly supervisor could be pointing out procedures to an Indian line worker, while a German quality officer could be conducting an interview. Trained professional interpreters are being recruited to work on manufacturing projects for weeks or even months at a time. Having an interpreter on the ground ensures effective communication in training, safety, and maintenance meetings, as well as troubleshooting when ideas are brought up, experts say. Having a business partner in the room helps to achieve more, fewer errors, and hopefully a better work environment.ConclusionAs India accelerates its growth as a Global manufacturing leader, the need for proficient foreign language interpreters and a reliable expert localization partner to be experienced at all levels of the industry is likely to increase significantly. Following the rise of marketplace translation, technical translation service, business translation services, legal translation services, and certified translation services, truly abreast manufacturing industries, it is going to be essential that firms dealing with global suppliers, engineers, regulators, and investors fully understand how to offer correct translation and their business translation needs on time.As the world is moving towards a more integrated industrial world, CMM Languages has become one of the most trusted foreign language interpreters and localization service providers on behalf of Indian and Multinational companies serving the industries related to manufacturing, engineering, automotive, pharmaceutical, and other industries. With its proven competencies in multilingual interpretation, technical document translation, legal localisation, and certified language solutions, the company is assisting the Indian and the Multinational manufacturers to cater to the English and the Indian market.(ADVERTORIAL DISCLAIMER: The above press release has been provided by VMPL. title: بنسبة ارتفاع 7 . 1 ٪ عن الربع الرابع من 2025 .. فى تقرير لـ « معلومات مجلس الوزراء »: 12 مليار دولار صادرات مصر « غير البترولية »
raw_text:
أصدر مركز المعلومات ودعم اتخاذ القرار بمجلس الوزراء، العدد 20 من تقرير «الصادرات السلعية غير البترولية»، وهى إصدارة ربع سنوية تتناول نظرة عامة على هيكل الميزان التجار غير البترولى المصرى خلال الفترة (الربع الرابع 2024 - الربع الرابع 2025)، بالإضافة إلى تطور الصادرات السلعية غير البترولية عن الفترة المذكورة، كما تتناول عرضًا للعلاقات التجارية بين مصر وأهم الشركاء التجاريين خلال الفترة (الربع الرابع 2024 - الربع الرابع 2025).

وبلغت قيمة صادرات مصر من السلع غير البترولية 12 مليار دولار خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025 مقابل نحو 11.2 مليار دولار خلال الربع نفسه من عام 2024، بنسبة ارتفاع بلغت نحو 7.1%. فيما بلغت قيمة الواردات المصرية من السلع غير البترولية 23.3 مليار دولار خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025، مقابل نحو 21.2 مليار دولار خلال الربع نفسه من عام 2024، بنسبة ارتفاع بلغت نحو 9.9%، وفقاً لبيانات الهيئة العامة للرقابة على الصادرات والواردات.

واستعرض التقرير تطور قيمة الصادرات المصرية من السلع غير البترولية وفقًا لأعلى مجموعات السلع تصديرًا خلال الربع الرابع 2025، حيث جاءت مجموعة اللؤلؤ الطبيعى أو المستنبت والأحجار الكريمة فى مقدمة الصادرات المصرية من السلع غير البترولية من حيث القيمة خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025، وذلك بنحو 1.3 مليار دولار مقابل نحو 1.1 مليار دولار خلال الربع نفسه من عام 2024، تلتها صادرات مجموعة الآلات والأجهزة والمعدات الكهربائية وأجزاؤها بقيمة 891.1 مليون دولار خلال الربع الرابع من عام 2025، مقابل نحو 764.3 مليون دولار خلال الربع نفسه من عام 2024.

title: Flexitank Market 2026 - 2035 : Growth Forecast , Leading Manufacturers , and Operational Safety Insights
raw_text:
Qingdao, Shandong, China, June 22, 2026 -- A newly published industry report from Spherical Insights & Consulting indicates that the global flexitank market is entering a sustained period of expansion, with the sector projected to grow from USD 1.5 billion in 2024 to USD 7.6 billion by 2035, at a CAGR of 15.9%. The findings reflect a broader structural shift in bulk liquid logistics, driven by rising global trade of food-grade and non-hazardous liquids, increasing adoption of flexible logistics solutions, and growing preference for single-use, contamination-free transport systems. Over the past decade, flexitanks have transformed from a niche packaging solution into a mainstream logistics asset, offering lower shipping costs, higher container utilization, and an improved environmental footprint compared with ISO tanks and drums. For shippers seeking reliable flexitank manufacturers the market now offers extensive options from best flexitank brands worldwide.

According to multiple industry research firms, the market outlook remains strongly positive.

Expert Market Research valued the market at USD 1,384 million in 2025, projecting USD 9,083 million by 2035 (CAGR ~20.7%).

Precedence Research estimates USD 2.07 billion in 2025, reaching USD 13.70 billion by 2035 (CAGR 20.8%).

SNS Insider reports USD 1.74 billion in 2025, expected to reach USD 13.1 billion by 2035 (CAGR 23.1%).

While forecasts vary, the consensus is clear: the flexitank market is experiencing sustained double-digit growth through 2035.

Global edible oil trade exceeded 200 million tonnes in 2024, creating sustained demand for bulk liquid transport. The shift from ISO tanks to flexible systems eliminates cleaning costs and empty returns, reducing shipping costs by up to 35%. ESG regulations favor lightweight containers that reduce fuel consumption and CO₂ emissions. Growth of China-Europe liquid export routes and expansion of chemical supply chains are also driving adoption.

Asia-Pacific dominates with over 46% market share in 2025. China remains the largest production hub, home to many China flexitank suppliers, and best China flexitank factories.

North America is the fastest-growing market, with the U.S. market expected to reach USD 2.62 billion by 2035 (CAGR 22.4%).

Europe maintains strong demand from wine and beverage industries, with 2.5 billion liters of wine shipped via flexitanks in 2024.

Middle East & Africa and Latin America

Middle East & Africa and Latin America show the highest growth, driven by agricultural liquid exports.

Industry Trends Shaping 2026-2035

Advanced Barrier Film Technology

Multi-layer polyethylene and EVOH barrier films improve oxygen resistance, chemical stability, and temperature tolerance (-20°C to 65°C).

IoT-enabled sensors provide real-time temperature, pressure, and liquid level monitoring.

Biodegradable and recyclable materials are increasingly prioritized in response to sustainability mandates from major FMCG companies. Standard flexitanks are single-use packaging, ensuring hygiene and preventing cross-contamination. Their sustainability lies in recyclable materials, reduced waste, and lower emissions per ton-kilometer.

Leading manufacturers adopt AI-based leak testing and 100% raw material traceability.

Leading Manufacturers in the Global Flexitank Industry

Key players in the flexitank manufacturers list include:

China-Qingdao LAF Technology (large-scale, edible oils, wine flexitanks); Qingdao BLT /Uni Flexitank/Yunjet (OEM/ODM); Hengxin (wine flexitanks); Zhongxiang/Trust (trailer and reefer flexitanks).

Safety and Operational Standards

Is a Flexitank Safe? Damage Rate & Container Bulging

Industry data shows approximately 4% of shipments in 2024 experienced minor leakage or bulging. Over 90% are attributed to operational errors: sharp container edges, overloading beyond 26,000 liters, missing door bars, and unskilled installation. Container bulging occurs when door bars are missing. The Container Owners Association (COA) has established stringent guidelines for production, installation, and use. Choosing reliable flexitank manufacturers is essential for minimizing risk.

What Liquids Can Be Transported?

Flexitanks handle non-hazardous bulk liquids across multiple categories. Food-grade liquids include edible oils, wine, fruit juice, syrup, dairy products, and honey - certified under FDA, FSSC 22000, HALAL, and KOSHER. Industrial oils include lubricants, glycerin, and base oils. Non-hazardous chemicals include latex, emulsions, and water-based adhesives. Specialized applications include bitumen with heat-resistant liners up to 120°C (248°F). Flexitanks are not suitable for dangerous goods (Class 1-9 hazardous materials) - ISO tanks remain standard for such cargo. Leading edible oil flexitank manufacturers, wine flexitank manufacturers, juice flexitank manufacturers, latex flexitank manufacturers, lubricant flexitank manufacturers, palm oil flexitank manufacturers, and bitumen flexitank manufacturers offer specialized solutions for each application.

Cost Savings: Flexitank vs. IBC vs. ISO Tank

A standard 20ft flexitank holds 14,000-26,000 liters, replacing 24-30 steel drums or one ISO tank. Flexitanks lower shipping costs by up to 30%: $1,200-$1,800 per 24,000L shipment with no cleaning and no empty return. IBC totes (24 units) cost $3,500-$4,200 with cleaning and return costs. ISO tank rentals cost $2,000-$2,800 with cleaning and return costs. 20ft flexitank manufacturers typically offer 14,000-26,000L, while 40ft flexitank manufacturers provide up to 28,000L high-capacity models.

Installation, Unloading & Temperature Range

Is flexitank installation difficult? Proper installation is critical. Steps: inspect container; place cardboard lining; insert flexitank; secure door end with baffle and bulkhead. Professional installation is strongly recommended. Missing door bars, overloading, and poor container condition account for 90% of leaks. What is the unloading residue rate of a flexitank? Below 0.5% for high-viscosity liquids. Can a flexitank transport hot or cold liquids? Standard range is -25°C to 60°C; heat-resistant liners withstand up to 120°C. Reefer flexitank manufacturers provide solutions for refrigerated containers. Valve types include butterfly, ball, and pinch. Food-grade certifications include FSSC 22000, FDA 21 CFR, EU 10/2011, HALAL, KOSHER, ISO 9001, and ISO 14001. Flexitanks are 100% recyclable; used liners reprocessed into pallets and construction materials.

Key developments include IoT-enabled smart tracking with real-time monitoring of temperature, pressure, and liquid level; fully recyclable and biodegradable liners driven by sustainability mandates; AI-driven load optimization for safer logistics; expansion in Africa and Latin America opening new export routes; 40ft flexitank adoption addressing 20ft container shortages and long-distance rail needs; and automated loading and unloading solutions reducing manual handling risks.

By 2035, flexitanks are expected to become the dominant global solution for non-hazardous liquid bulk shipping under 30,000 liters.

title: Why Canada has generic Ozempic , and the US doesnt
raw_text:
Experts say the Canadian generics may also be eyed by patients in the US, where Ozempic costs upwards of US$1,000 per month.

Elizabeth Doran has been taking GLP-1 medications for nearly a year for weight loss to help reverse her prediabetes and high blood pressure. Because she had not yet developed diabetes, the retired 69-year-old was prescribed Wegovy for weight loss rather than its sister drug, Ozempic – both of which contain the active ingredient semaglutide.

"I was one decimal point away from being diabetic," Doran, who lives in Ottawa, Canada, told the BBC.

Her Wegovy prescription meant she was not eligible for insurance drug coverage offered to diabetic seniors in Ontario, forcing her to pay between C$350 ($250; £188) to C$500 out of pocket a month.

To afford the medication, Doran said she picked up substitute teaching shifts a few times a month. She also used discount cards offered by the drug's manufacturer, Novo Nordisk, and took advantage of a first-month free offer through her doctor.

But Doran may no longer have to pay such a steep price or hunt for a bargain.

In May, Canada became the first country in the G7 to approve a generic semaglutide injection, intended for type 2 diabetes patients but can be prescribed off-label for weight loss. The discounted medications are expected to be in pharmacies across the country as of the beginning of June, at less than a third of the cost.

The arrival of the generics has the potential to make GLP-1 drugs more accessible to the three million Canadians who take them, as well as to many others who have considered it but resisted because of the price. It has already forced Novo Nordisk to lower prices of their brand-name drugs.

Experts say the Canadian generics may also be eyed by patients in the US, where Ozempic costs upwards of US$1,000 per month for uninsured Americans, and where low-cost alternatives are not expected to arrive on the market for a few more years due to drug patent laws that allow companies to maintain a monopoly for longer. More than 15 million American adults are estimated to take GLP-1 medications.

Canada's approval of the generic GLP-1s comes after India this year approved dozens of low-cost versions, causing a price scramble that has prompted Novo Nordisk to cut the prices of Ozempic and Wegovy by nearly 50% in that country.

Generic Ozempic by two manufacturers has already been approved by Health Canada – one by India-based pharmaceutical company Dr Reddy's and another by Canadian company Apotex.

Erez Israeli, CEO of Dr Reddy's, told the BBC that his company had applied for approval in more than 80 countries, including the US. In addition to Canada, he expects Dr Reddy's generic GLP-1 will soon be available in South America, Africa and most of Asia – but not in the US, UK or Europe.

Meanwhile, Apotex has secured a tentative approval by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), though it is not able to sell its generic semaglutide drug there yet.

US and European countries allow for companies to extend their patents for several years as a way to compensate them for regulatory delays, explained Tahir Amin, CEO and founder of US-based group the Initiative for Medicines, Access & Knowledge (I-MAK), which advocates for drug patent reform.

Amin said Americans would not see a generic until 2032, when the main compound patent protecting semaglutide is expected to expire.

Novo Nordisk's patent on Ozempic could have been extended until 2028 in Canada but the company failed to renew it, Amin said. It is unclear why, he added, but "somebody dropped the ball … that's why you've got generics in Canada sooner".

Novo Nordisk said in a statement that the introduction generics in Canada was a "localized situation based on our specific patent timelines and regulatory environment and does not reflect the situation in the United States, where exclusivity remains intact".

Amin said there were likely conversations already swirling among Americans on how they could access low-cost generic Ozempic from Canada.

It wouldn't be the first time Americans sought access to lower cost drugs north of the border. In 2019, a self-described "caravan" of Americans bused to Canada to purchase cheaper insulin for type 1 diabetes - and to protest the costs in the US for the life-saving medication.

In 2023, the province of British Columbia put restrictions on Americans purchasing its Ozempic after it found that 15% of prescriptions for the drug came from the US, mostly through Canada-based online pharmacies.

The practice was condemned by the former provincial health minister at the time.

"The purpose of procuring Ozempic for British Columbia patients is not to turn around and export it right back to the United States," said then-health minister Adrian Dix.

For Canadians like Doran, the introduction of generics to Canada's market is "huge". It means being able to maintain the weight she has lost at a fraction of the cost, she said, while keeping diabetes and heart disease at bay.

"By taking this drug, I'm probably saving the healthcare system a lot of money," Doran said. She added she had already noticed the price of Wegovy drop since the generics were approved.

Esther Linetsky, another Canadian patient who was prescribed Ozempic for weight loss, said the high cost forced her to get off the drug temporarily and later ration free samples of both Wegovy and Ozempic that were provided to her by her doctor.

"My doctor wanted me to go up to the next dose, but going up to the next dose meant increasing my cost, and I couldn't afford to do it," she told the BBC.

With the generics, Linetsky said she hoped she can go back to using the drugs the way they were intended – and at a more affordable price tag.

In the US, the higher prices mean that GLP-1 drugs have mostly been accessed by those who are wealthier, leaving people who especially need it to manage their diabetes unable to secure it, said Amin from I-MAK.

He added that changing the patent system in the US was an uphill battle, calling it the "Golden Egg" of the pharmaceutical industry, which he said had aggressively lobbied and litigated for the status quo to remain.

Novo Nordisk most recently took American online pharmacy Hims and Hers to court for selling compounded versions of semaglutide at a lower cost. The legal battle was dropped in March after the pharmacy agreed to stop advertising the compounds and sell semaglutide under the Ozempic and Wegovy brand. It has also fought to have its patent extended in other countries, like China and Brazil.

Martin Arès, CEO of the Canadian pharmaceutical company Apotex, said he was exploring ways to bring his generic product to Americans now that it had been tentatively approved by the FDA.

He contends that it definitely will not be on the US market this year.

"But we remain committed to bringing this product as soon as possible," Arès said, adding that the company had experts working on identifying ways to make that happen.

Research reveals genetic factors influence weight loss effectiveness of drugs like Wegovy and Mounjaro. Study shows varied results among users. Learn more.

It’s not just what you eat, but how you think about it that matters.

The Federal Reserve's hawkish stance continues to support the US dollar and keeps global investors cautious.

Asian markets are trading with a negative bias this morning, led by weakness in Japanese equities as the technology sell-off persists. However, the continued decline in Brent crude towards $72 per barrel is a positive for India, easing concerns around inflation and the current account.

From a technical perspective, the broader trend remains positive as long as the Nifty sustains above the 24,000 mark. Immediate resistance is placed at 24,200, and a decisive breakout above this level could trigger fresh momentum towards 24,400. On the downside, 23,800 remains a crucial support; a breach could lead to a corrective move towards 23,600.
